goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

outcome.reason: Reached the payment step. Stopped there: nothing was paid.

findings.problem: Home page has about 20 tab stops (header links, search, menu, six promo banners, an unnamed link) before the first product; the menu list took one tab stop and I could not reach individual menu items.

element.name: What is new Women Men Gear Training Sale

findings.problem: Size and Color swatches gave no feedback when I pressed Enter or Space. I could not tell whether anything was selected until I saw Size XS and Color Blue in the cart. The Color swatches were announced only as Color, Blue, Orange, Purple, with no visible text.

After Add to Cart, focus stayed on the product button, now labelled Added. The cart link in the confirmation message was about 20 shift-tabs back, and the mini-cart link in the header was equally far. A keyboard user has to tab back through every swatch and banner to reach the cart.
Checkout page was blank at first. Focus started on the store logo and Sign In before the form, and the email tooltip and phone tooltip were separate unnamed tab stops that did not say what they were.

State/Province dropdown was long and could only be filled by typing the name, and the Country list has over 240 entries. Shipping method radios were separate tab stops with no group label heard, so Next was not obvious.
After Next, the payment form appeared lower on the same page and focus went back to the top of the page. I got no announcement that the payment step had opened.
